What we are looking for

Aurora hires talented people with diverse backgrounds who are ready to help build a transportation ecosystem that will make our roads safer, get crucial goods where they need to go, and make mobility more efficient and accessible for all.

 

We’re looking for a Staff Application Security Engineer with a strong software engineering background to help build and maintain an AI-native application security program for our driverless truck product and supporting infrastructure. This is a builder-first role for someone who enjoys understanding complex systems and working alongside engineers to improve them. You’ll collaborate on fixes and design-level improvements, build automation, and make security a low-friction part of the software development lifecycle. You’ll use AI thoughtfully to scale your attention while applying your own engineering judgment.

 

In this role you will

 

 - Partner with engineering teams on fixes and secure design improvements, contributing code directly.

 - Investigate findings and their practical impact, bringing clear evidence and possible solutions when engaging the responsible teams.

 - Help build and maintain the application security program and its tooling, using AI to scale investigation while validating results.

 - Build automation and integrate preventative controls into the software development lifecycle to reduce recurring risks and friction.

 

Required qualifications

 

 - 8+ years of experience in security , applications security engineering, or product security roles 

 - Substantial experience building and maintaining production software, with strong programming, debugging, and system design skills.

 - Ability to investigate unfamiliar codebases, understand system behavior, and reason about potential misuse.

 - Experience delivering technical work across teams in a large or complex engineering organization.

 - Demonstrated ability to threat model systems, explain technical risks, and tradeoffs clearly and collaborate with engineers on practical solutions.

 - Experience building developer tooling, automation, or software development lifecycle integrations.

 - Practical experience using AI to support technical work, with the judgment to validate its output and explain the underlying reasoning.

 - Experience with languages in our stack: C, C++, Go, Python, JavaScript, and web frameworks.

 

Desirable qualifications

 

 - Hands-on experience building or maintaining both cloud and embedded systems, ideally with deep technical knowledge of each.

 - Experience developing software for safety-critical products or their supporting infrastructure, particularly autonomous vehicle technology.

 - Application or product security experience, including in-depth code audits, secure design reviews, threat modeling, or vulnerability investigation.

 - Experience building and maintaining production AI-assisted security tooling or automation.

Aurora hires talented people with diverse backgrounds who are ready to help build a transportation ecosystem that will make our roads safer, get crucial goods where they need to go, and make mobility more efficient and accessible for all.  We are seeking a highly motivated CDL A professional to join our Autonomous Vehicle (AV) testing team. In this role, you aren’t just a driver—you are a vital part of our development process. You will operate Class 8 trucks equipped with cutting-edge self-driving technology to help us map, test, and build the future of transportation. This role is built for those who love the open road and is perfect for individuals comfortable with up to 90% travel.

We are currently hiring at our Houston, Texas terminal. Houston: PM Shift: Thursday - Monday

Employment Type: This is a 12-month assignment with the potential to extend.

In this role, you will

 - Strictly adhere to all safety protocols and DOT regulations while acting as a professional representative of the company to the public.

 - Operate the truck while following specific, technical driving protocols to collect high-quality data for our engineering teams.

 - At times work as a two-person team, cross-training to sit in the passenger seat, where you will manage mission software, troubleshoot equipment, and monitor real-time data feeds.

 - Execute test missions to evaluate software changes on public roads and closed courses, acting as the "eyes and ears" for our engineers.

 - Perform Pre-Trips—going beyond standard DOT/FMCSA inspections to verify sensor calibrations and ensure software is updated for the day’s mission.

 - Use onboard digital tools to "flag" or "tag" road events (like construction or unique traffic behaviors) so engineers can review the data later.

 - Perform simple troubleshooting, such as restarting software modules or checking sensor connections with remote guidance from our engineering team.

Who You Are

 - A Continuous Learner: You don't need a computer science degree, but you must be comfortable using laptops/tablets and eager to build a foundation in autonomous technology.

 - A Growth Mindset: You value coaching and feedback and are excited by the fast-moving nature of the AV industry.

 - Detail Oriented: You take pride in providing clear, actionable feedback on how the truck "feels" and behaves on the road.

Required Qualifications

Licensing & Compliance:

 - Interstate Class-A Commercial Driver's License (CDL)

 - Valid U.S. Driver’s License (in addition to the CDL)

 - Must pass DOT physical and meet all DOT qualification standards.

 - Must pass pre-employment, post-incident, and randomized drug testing in accordance with FMCSA requirements

 - Driving record must pass Motor Vehicle Report (MVR) guidelines

 - Is at least 25 years of age

Experience & Technical Skills:

 - Minimum 3 years of experience driving trucks commercially 

 - Demonstrated mechanical aptitude for basic troubleshooting and maintenance of vehicle systems

 - Proficiency in collaboration tools, including Google Docs, Slides, and Sheets

 - Experience with Jira (e.g., filling out tickets, tracking ticket statuses)

Aptitude & Soft Skills:

 - Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, for technical reporting and team collaboration

 - Ability to use laptops and tablets to launch test missions, monitor real-time data feeds, and enter detailed digital logs.

 - Inquisitive attitude, interested in problem solving and solving puzzles

 - Positive experiences working in a collaborative environment - team player

 - Ability to prioritize and make strategic decisions proactively 

 - Demonstrated mechanical aptitude for basic troubleshooting and maintenance

Work Environment & Travel:

 - Comfortable with long distance driving in diverse traffic and weather conditions

 - Ability to travel weekly to new collection locations (up to 90% of the time)

 - Comfortable with air travel for deployments

 - Ability to work rotating shifts as needed, and regular overtime and weekends

Desirable Qualifications

 - Experience in an Agile or Scrum Environment

 - Experience with Linux or Command Line Interfaces (CLI)

 - Prior Experience in Aviation, or High-Stakes Logistics

 - Experience with high-fidelity mapping tools and procedures

 - Experience in a safety-critical operations environment or vehicle development/testing

Work Environment and Requirements

 - Travel: Significant and frequent travel (up to 90%) across various domestic locations, often for extended periods over the road.

 - Environmental Exposure: 
   
   - Must be prepared to operate the Commercial Motor Vehicle (CMV) and execute mission protocols in a wide range of weather conditions (e.g., heat, cold, rain, snow) and diverse road environments (e.g., urban, rural, interstate highways, construction zones). 
   
   - Operators must be comfortable with exposure to dust, dirt, vibration, and other particulate matter common to commercial vehicle operations.

 - Schedule: Flexibility to work non-standard hours, including over the road schedules, weekends or nights, to meet critical development deadlines.

 - Testing: Ability to pass all DOT and company-required testing, including pre-employment drug and alcohol screening, ongoing random testing, and annual medical certification.

 - Physical Requirements: Ability to sit for long periods while operating a vehicle and the ability to lift up to 50 pounds for equipment handling and cargo securing.

 - Ability to work independently with minimal supervision

 - Available to work day or night shifts

 - Basic Knowledge of DOT and CVSA rules and requirements

 - Direct manufacturing and prototyping experience a bonus

 - Prior experience working with autonomous vehicles

 - Advanced CAN bus diagnostics and troubleshooting

 - Vehicle network communication diagnostics (CAN, J1939)

We’re searching for a Map Operations Specialist to join our Map Production team in Mountain View, CA. Map Production builds and maintains the HD semantic maps the Aurora Driver relies on to navigate safely from destination to destination. In this role, you will become an expert in Aurora’s mapping policies, processes, and proprietary tools, deliver high-quality map annotations, and grow into owning a functional area of the team, driving the documentation, process improvements, and automation that help our mapping operations scale.

In this role you will

 - Annotate, expand, and maintain HD semantic maps using Aurora’s proprietary mapping tools, meeting productivity and quality goals

 - Support day-to-day Production operations, including annotation queues, map issue escalations, construction-zone monitoring, and route launches

 - Manage your own workload across multiple processes and adapt to shifting priorities, escalating risks and blockers early

 - Take ownership of a functional area as a subject matter expert, building documentation, process flows, and best practices

 - Identify gaps in tools, workflows, and procedures, and drive improvements through optimization, scaling, and automation

 - Partner with Engineering, Enablement (Training), and functional owners to share feedback and improve mapping tools and processes

 - Mentor teammates by sharing best practices and leading shadow sessions

Required qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience

 - 4+ years of professional experience in operations, mapping/GIS, data annotation, or another technical operations environment

 - Strong attention to detail and the ability to deliver consistent quality on high-volume, policy-driven work

 - Hands-on troubleshooting skills and comfort working with technical tools and data

 - Clear written and verbal communication, including documenting processes and escalating issues

 - Ability to work onsite in Mountain View, CA, Monday through Friday (10AM–6:30PM PT)

Desirable qualifications

 - Technical skills such as SQL, scripting, or data analysis

 - Experience using AI tools to support daily work, such as data analysis or dashboard creation

 - Project management or team leadership experience

 - Experience with GIS, HD mapping, geospatial data, autonomous vehicles, or robotics

What we are looking for

We're searching for a Staff Cybersecurity Engineer to help mature Cloud & Enterprise Detection within our Detection & Response (D&R) team, under the Technical Assurance division. This is a senior individual contributor role focused on driving cross-functional projects that strengthen Aurora's detection infrastructure and expand detection coverage across our cloud infrastructure, enterprise environments. You will scope and lead multi-quarter initiatives that raise the maturity of our detection program and powering detection at scale, executing through your own hands-on work and through close partnership with Cloud Infrastructure, IT, and Platform Engineering teams.

In this role you will

 - Drive cross-functional projects to mature Aurora's detection infrastructure, log ingestion and normalization, detection-as-code pipelines with testing, versioning, and CI/CD for detection content, and scalable, cost-aware telemetry collection

 - Expand detection coverage across cloud and corporate environments and prioritize coverage improvements

 - Design, build, and tune detections for cloud control plane and workload activity, identity-based attacks, endpoint,  SaaS threats, abuse of CI/CD and service-to-service communication paths

 - Partner with Cloud Infrastructure, IT, and Platform Engineering to embed logging and detection requirements into system design, and represent D&R in cross-functional working groups and design reviews

 - Integrate threat intelligence and adversary emulation into detection coverage priorities, and conduct proactive threat hunting across cloud, identity, endpoint, and SaaS data

 - Respond to cloud and enterprise security incidents and participate in an on-call rotation, feeding lessons learned back into detection coverage and infrastructure improvements

 - Collaborate with and mentor SOC engineers on cloud and enterprise detection practices, and contribute to quarterly planning for detection infrastructure and coverage initiatives

Required qualifications

 - 10+ years of security experience; demonstrated experience leading cross-functional security projects or programs from scoping through delivery

 - Strong technical foundation in threat detection, incident response

 - Expertise with cloud security across one or more major providers, including cloud-native telemetry and detection sources

 - Experience building or maturing detection infrastructure - SIEM or security data lake pipelines, log onboarding and normalization, detection-as-code workflows

 - Expertise with endpoint detection and response (EDR) and SaaS security monitoring, or comparable host and application telemetry depth

 - Expertise authoring and maintaining detections (anomalous, network, host, identity, or cloud activity) and measuring detection coverage against adversary behavior

 - Experience with incident management, driving cross-departmental collaboration for containment and remediation

 - Expertise with MITRE ATT&CK framework and modern adversarial techniques; understanding of NIST CSF

 - Ability to write quality, testable code in Python

Desirable qualifications

 - Experience designing and implementing Zero Trust Architecture

 - Experience scaling SOC, Detection Engineering with AI/LLM

 - Experience building and architecting data lakes

 - Experience with compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001)

What we are looking for

We’re searching for a Senior Software Engineer, ML Evaluation & Introspection Infrastructure to join our Behavior Analysis team, reporting to the team’s engineering manager. Aurora’s trucks already haul freight on Texas highways with no one on board, and every new version of the learned model that drives them has to prove, on real driving data, that it is better and safer than the one before. Behavior Analysis builds the systems that make that call: the evals that compare model versions, the embedding search that makes every driving scenario findable, and the introspection tools that show why a model did what it did. Engineers build more than 100 training and eval datasets a week through our tools. We’re a small team, so each engineer owns whole systems, and we work agent-first: our tools are built for AI agents to drive as easily as engineers do. You’ll own core pieces of that loop and help lead what comes next: putting LLMs, VLMs and agents to work on analysis, so questions that take days to answer today take minutes.

In this role you will

 - Build and scale evaluation pipelines that compare model versions on large driving datasets: offline evals, slice-based metrics, regression detection, and model-vs-model reports.

 - Own embedding and vector-search pipelines over driving data, versioned per model, so engineers can search, cluster and compare how any model represents the world. This is where you’d start: owning embedding generation and search end to end.

 - Build model introspection infrastructure (attention, attribution, ablations) that turns “why did the model do that?” from a research project into a query.

 - Help define how frontier LLMs, VLMs and agents change ML analysis here: triaging, labeling, clustering and summarizing driving scenarios and eval results. We already have a prototype using LLMs for data curation, and you’d help decide where it goes next.

 - Work side by side with the ML engineers training these models to decide what to measure, then make those measurements trustworthy, observable and cheap enough to run on every candidate model.

 - Build the web app and CLI that engineers and AI agents use to find datasets, training runs, evals and their costs, designed with agents as first-class users.

Required qualifications

 - Typically 5+ years of professional software engineering experience building backend, data or ML infrastructure.

 - Strong Python, and proficiency with SQL.

 - Designed and operated large-scale batch or data pipelines on cloud infrastructure, including backfills, retries and cost management.

 - Built systems that measure or evaluate something: metrics, experimentation, evaluation or analytics platforms.

 - Experience with distributed compute and container orchestration (e.g. Kubernetes, AWS Batch or similar).

Desirable qualifications

 - ML evaluation infrastructure: eval harnesses, golden datasets, regression detection, A/B model comparison.

 - Embeddings and vector search, or model introspection and interpretability tooling.

 - Using LLMs, VLMs or agentic workflows to automate analysis, labeling or data curation.

 - Autonomous vehicles, robotics or other large-scale sensor data.

 - Observability for data systems (metrics, alerting, SLOs), and everyday use of AI coding agents.

 - Coming from backend or data engineering and want to learn ML evaluation? Apply anyway: we’ll teach you the ML side.

   - Build and improve model pipelines for large-scale and efficient model training.
   
   - Analyze failure modes and implementation/testing of solutions to address the surfaced issues

 - Hands-on experience with VLM, foundational or world models.

Aurora's Product Operations team is at the fore-front of technology, providing partnership to product, operations & engineering and ensuring commercial operations capabilities are delivered on time, safely and efficiently. Within Product Operations, our Software Product & Release Operations function owns the release cadence and readiness of everything Aurora ships in software — closing the gap between engineering roadmaps and operational readiness, not just reporting on it.

We're searching for an innovative, solutions-oriented leader to own the software release cycle end-to-end, from build readiness through rollout, as Aurora ramps production toward 20 AVs deployed per week following our first AAET launch. This role partners closely with Aurora Driver and Service Engineering , Launch Operations, and Product Ops & Platform Enablement. You'll be both the accountable owner of software Go/No-Go decisions and the primary translator of engineering roadmaps into an operational readiness plan the rest of Product Operations can plan against. To be successful in this role, you need to pair technical fluency in software release management with a data-driven outlook, exceptional communication skills with strong executive presence, the ability to bring ambiguity into focus in a fast-paced environment, and the ability to influence stakeholders without direct authority.

You will report directly to the Senior Director, Product Operations, and be based in San Francisco, Pittsburgh or Dallas, with willingness to travel to test sites and partner facilities as needed.

In this role you will:

 - Own Enterprise-Wide Customer and Operations Release Strategy: Own and evolve the overarching operations release strategy across software, autonomous systems, and fleet operations, ensuring our release and rollout framework scales seamlessly with business and fleet growth.

 - Define Release Operational readiness & risk Governance: Define and institute company-wide release readiness and risk gating standards, serving as the accountable authority for the evaluation framework leadership relies on to clear commercial deployments.

 - Drive Cross-Functional Capability Roadmap Alignment: Partner directly with VP and Director-level leaders across Engineering, Product, and Commercial Operations to align multi-year capability roadmaps with commercial and business GTM expansion targets.

 - Unify Multi-System Releases: Unify release governance across complex, interdependent software, hardware, and platform changes—resolving top-level trade-offs and cross-departmental dependencies when release timelines conflict with operational readiness

 - Establish Customer & Operations Release & Health Metrics: Define, own, and report on enterprise release predictability, defect escape metrics, and roadmap-to-readiness lead times for executive leadership.

 - Manage Feature & Defect Escalation Frameworks: Standardize backlog hygiene and defect escalation pathways across the software and operational release pipelines, ensuring systemic feedback loops exist between field performance and engineering.

 - Own the Software Release and change Management Cycle: Own and evolve the overall release strategy across autonomous operations. Spanning across the entire software release cycle, from build readiness through rollout, in partnership with Software Engineering.

 - Manage Feature and Bug Tracking: Own backlog hygiene and defect escalation paths across the software release pipeline, ensuring nothing falls through the cracks between Engineering and Operations.

 - Coordinate on Mixed Releases: Partner with Product Ops & Platform Enablement on releases that span both software and hardware/platform changes, deferring Go/No-Go authority to them for the hardware/platform components.

 - Drive Release Metrics: Own and report on release predictability, defect escape rate, and roadmap-to-readiness lead time.

Required Qualifications:

 - 7+ years of experience in program/product operations, technical program management, or release management, ideally in a software-driven environment with adjacent hardware dependencies (automotive, robotics, or similar)

 - Demonstrated experience owning a software release cycle end-to-end, including build readiness, rollout, and defect management

 - Proven track record of building or improving feature and bug tracking systems and processes at scale

 - Strong cross-functional stakeholder management — this role sits between Engineering and Operations and needs credibility with both

 - Comfort operating in a fast-scaling, R&D-to-commercial transition environment — someone who builds repeatable process without over-engineering it around a moving technical target

 - Strong analytical and communication skills, able to translate technical release data into clear, actionable recommendations for both technical and executive audiences

Desired Qualifications:

 - Experience in autonomous vehicles, automotive, or another safety-critical software domain

 - Familiarity with how software releases interact with hardware/platform dependencies, even without owning that release cycle directly

 - Background in technical program management or software release engineering

 - Experience working with BI tools (Tableau, Looker, PowerBI, etc.) for release metrics tracking

 - Familiarity with Jira, Confluence, or equivalent tools for release and backlog tracking

What we are looking for

Aurora's commercial trucking network is expanding. By the end of 2026, more than 200 Aurora-powered trucks will be in driverless commercial operation across multiple freight corridors. Every new lane, endpoint, weigh station, and truck stop must clear software readiness gates spanning map development, ODD analysis, test creation, and on-road performance before it can carry commercial freight without a driver.

The Staff PM, Network Expansion owns that picture. This role is the primary source of truth for software readiness across all active and upcoming sites, and is responsible for making that state legible to senior leadership, commercial partners, and the engineering teams accountable for closing gaps. The work requires strong technical understanding of the software readiness process, tight coordination across Mapping, Perception, Motion Planning, Systems & Safety Engineering, and Vehicle Operations, and direct engagement with Business Development and Product Strategy to connect readiness to commercial priorities.

The commercial network will be materially larger in 18 months than it is today. A significant part of this role is building the processes and tooling to scale with it.

In this role you will

 - Software Readiness Ownership: Own the definitive view of where every highway segment, customer endpoint, weigh station, border patrol station, and truck stop stands against software readiness criteria and customer commitments. This spans map development timelines, ODD analysis progress, test creation status, and on-road performance. Keep this picture current across all active sites and ensure it is the basis for release planning and prioritization decisions.

 - Program Synthesis and Executive Reporting: Aggregate workstream status across the lane expansion program and produce the executive software readiness update for senior leadership. Own the agenda and content for the weekly program review. Prepare and lead VP-level decision meetings when major risks require escalation or tradeoffs need to be resolved. The output of this work is senior leadership having an accurate, decision-ready view of the commercial network at all times.

 - Autonomy Roadmap and Commercial Alignment: Connect commercial network priorities to autonomy capability development. Partner with Perception, Motion Planning, and Systems & Safety Engineering to ensure the capability roadmap reflects the lanes and endpoints Aurora needs to open next. Partner with Business Development and Product Strategy to understand which sites carry the highest commercial priority and translate that into concrete input for engineering planning. When workstream slips affect the commercial schedule, articulate the business consequence clearly and identify available tradeoffs.

 - Cross-Program Execution: Track and unblock the engineering dependencies that determine when lanes and endpoints are ready to open. Work directly with Motion Planning, Perception, and Systems & Safety Engineering to understand capability timelines and surface gaps that affect the expansion schedule. Work with Mapping Operations to ensure mapping work is sequenced for lane and endpoint readiness timelines. Coordinate with Vehicle Operations to ensure efficient and effective on road testing.

 - Vehicle Demand Forecast: Partner with Vehicle Operations leadership to develop the fleet demand forecast, informing hiring decisions and vehicle allocation. Provide forward-looking input on which lanes and endpoints will require development vehicles and when.

 - Operational Infrastructure:Identify where current tracking and coordination processes will not scale as the network grows. Design and drive improvements to tooling and handoffs. The right person in this role will make it materially easier, a year from now, to answer "are we ready?" across a significantly larger set of routes.

Required Qualifications

 - Range across strategy and execution: This role requires both executive-level synthesis and hands-on operational work. Strong candidates can structure a prioritization framework for a VP audience and, in the same week, build a readiness checklist, run a daily check-in, or reconcile a tracking artifact manually. The role does not have a support layer for operational work.

 - Credibility with engineering teams: Must understand enough about ODD analysis, test coverage, and system integration to identify when a schedule is unrealistic, determine which risks belong in an executive update, and ask effective questions in engineering reviews. This is not a role for a generalist who relies on engineers to interpret technical state.

 - Cross-functional influence in high-stakes environments: Vehicle Operations, Mapping Operations, Systems & Safety Engineering, Perception, and Business Development each have their own leadership and competing priorities. Must be able to drive alignment and accountability across these organizations without owning their roadmaps. Experience navigating multi-team environments where you are accountable for outcomes you don't directly control is essential.

 - Comfort building in ambiguous environments: The processes and tooling for tracking a network of this scale are still being developed. Strong candidates treat this as core work, not a gap to work around.

 - Experience with operational or physical readiness programs (autonomous vehicles, aviation, rail, logistics, or manufacturing launch) is a plus.

 - Onboard into and help refine commercial command-center best practices, mirroring those workflows for development use cases

 - Provide structured feedback on feature/tool performance and report findings to Testing Program Managers

 - Respond to trigger requests/emergencies and safely send remote commands

 - Escalate complex or persistent issues to Vehicle Reliability Engineering (VRE) with complete documentation, following formal escalation procedures

 - Work as a team, win together, and serve as an ambassador for Aurora when interacting with the public

 - Flexibility for day/night/weekend work on a 4x10 schedule

Aurora's Finance Center of Excellence (COE) functions as an internal strategic advisory team. Rather than sitting permanently within a single siloed function, COE analysts build 360-degree business fluency across Aurora's business and are deployed where their analytical skills and business acumen add the most strategic value, gaining direct exposure to senior executive leadership while solving Aurora's highest-priority growth challenges.

As a Corporate FP&A Senior Analyst, a high-impact individual contributor role, you will directly support Aurora's company-wide financial planning and reporting processes — partnering with functional executive leaders across the organization to build budgets, manage capital allocation, and deliver key analytical deliverables for C-suite and Board-level decisions. We're looking for a self-motivated analyst who excels at translating complex operational details into clear financial narratives for executive audiences.

In this role, you will

 - Drive the consolidated company-wide annual budget, quarterly re-forecasts, and long-range financial planning (3-statement modeling) across corporate and operating functions;

 - Partner directly with department leaders to build, maintain, and optimize operational expenditure (Opex), Capital Expenditure (Capex), and Headcount drivers;

 - Prepare comprehensive variance analysis (Actuals vs. Plan), trend reports, and operational insight packages for executive leadership during monthly and quarterly close cycles;

 - Support the preparation of quarterly Board of Directors presentations, executive financial decks, and quarterly earnings support materials;

 - Establish, monitor, and refine company-wide corporate financial KPIs to identify efficiency opportunities and optimize operating leverage;

 - Present corporate financial performance, variance drivers, and capital allocation recommendations to Finance and operational leadership;

 - Review FP&A SOPs, financial governance workflows, and budgeting systems to implement scalable best practices across the organization;

 - Drive system automation, data integrity, and model integration across corporate FP&A planning platforms (e.g., Pigment) and accounting systems (e.g., NetSuite);

 - As a member of the Finance COE, flex across high-impact concurrent projects and strategic finance workstreams as corporate priorities evolve.

Required Qualifications

 - 5+ years of relevant experience in Corporate FP&A, Strategic Finance, or Investment Banking/Corporate Finance at a public or high-growth company; public company experience with quarterly reporting cycles required;

 - Degree in Finance or a related quantitative field such as Business, Economics, Math, or Statistics;

 - Strong proficiency in corporate budgeting, 3-statement financial modeling, variance analysis, and accounting consolidation principles;

 - Proven track record of partnering with cross-functional executive stakeholders to manage budgets and streamline planning workflows;

 - Ability to pivot seamlessly between granular operational inputs and macro executive messaging;

 - Hands-on experience with modern financial planning software (e.g., Pigment, Anaplan, Adaptive) and ERP systems (e.g., NetSuite);

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with demonstrated experience building executive presentation decks;

 - Strong analytical capability and rigorous attention to detail;

 - Comfort operating within a Center of Excellence model, leading multiple projects across cross-functional priorities.

Desirable Qualifications

 - Hands-on experience with SQL and major BI visualization platforms (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, Looker) strongly preferred;

 - CPA, CFA, or MBA preferred;

 - Prior industry experience in autonomous technology, logistics, mobility, automotive, or high-tech manufacturing;

 - Experience supporting investor relations or earnings preparation in a matrixed public company.

The Control Tower Analyst is the real-time coordination hub for Aurora's supply chain. This role coordinates the movement of all vehicles, manages internal and external data exchanges, keeps internal stakeholders aligned, and directs warehousing and reverse logistics activity across the network.

The job works like air traffic control. You will switch between tasks, projects, stakeholders, and deliverables every few minutes. You need to know which issues are active fires, which ones will become fires, and which ones can wait. When an issue can wait, you design a solution for it before it lands.

Beyond daily execution, this role builds continuous improvement plans that move the overall supply chain toward maturity. You will work closely with Implementation Teams whenever critical system needs arise across ERP (NetSuite), EDI, and JIRA.

This role is built for someone who genuinely enjoys new technology. The right candidate runs toward emerging tools, including AI, automation, and new system capabilities, rather than waiting until they're mandated. They look for ways new technology can make coordination faster, more accurate, and more scalable, and they bring those ideas forward on their own.

Data Exchange & Systems Coordination

 - Adopt new tools quickly to manage processes where no safety net or established workflow exists

 - Coordinate warehousing activity and reverse logistics flows across Aurora sites and third-party partners

We’re searching for a Senior Program Manager, Test Execution (Weekend). Aurora's Product Operations team plays a critical role in turning development priorities into safe, executable testing outcomes. This role provides dedicated weekend and adjacent-day (Thursday - Monday) on-site coverage across all Development Testing Operations work-streams, ensuring engineering teams have consistent program management support.

This Program Manager acts as the single point of contact for all assigned engineering areas during the weekend window, standing in for the full team of workstream PMs. You are the first line of defense for test execution questions and escalations, the direct escalation point for on-site issues, and the bridge to leadership when problems can't be resolved.

This is functionally an irregular-operations (IROPs) role: the weekday team builds the plan, and you deliver it. The job isn't to wait for direction; it's to develop and work a known set of playbooks, make the call within defined limits, and know exactly when to pick up the phone to escalate.

This role requires breadth over depth: rather than owning a single engineering relationship, you need working fluency across all the workstreams the team supports so you can triage confidently on your own during the window when the rest of the team is offline.

In This Role, You Will

 - Serve as the direct escalation point for all Program Managers' workstreams during the Saturday-Sunday coverage window, resolving first-tier test execution questions and issues and looping in the right people (Engineering, Safety, Operations, leadership) when they exceed first-tier scope.

 - Own and execute pre-built response playbooks and flag gaps in those playbooks back to the weekday teams

 - Define and work within a decision-authority matrix: know without checking which calls you're empowered to make solo, which need a same-day heads-up to leadership, and which require an immediate escalation before proceeding.

 - Make real-time, hands-on calls on resource substitution — reassigning available assets, adjusting test sequencing, or re-routing around a blocked track/route — to keep the weekend plan moving without waiting for Monday.

 - Support test execution questions and escalations across the full breadth of engineering areas the team covers, not just a single workstream.

 - Review the previous week's plan against actual execution and author the weekly status/summary report on how the week went

 - Recommend and make pivots to the upcoming week's plan based on weekend execution results, blockers, and on-the-ground changes (weather, asset downtime, route/track issues).

 - Track and communicate blockers, delays, and anomalies to stakeholders in a timely manner, using judgment on when an issue needs to go straight to leadership versus being resolved at the PM level.

 - Maintain clear documentation of weekend decisions, pivots, and escalations so the Monday–Friday team has full continuity into the new week.

The mission of Aurora’s OneTech Security Product Management team is to embed security into every aspect of Aurora’s products—spanning software, hardware, and services. As a Staff Technical Product &Program Manager, Security, you will be responsible for driving security strategy and initiatives across the organization, ensuring that security is a fundamental and functional part of the Aurora product development process.

You will act as a bridge between Security and Product teams across the organization, moving seamlessly between high-level strategy and detailed execution to ensure that complex, cross-functional security is successfully integrated into products developed across the company. Your ability to lead, influence, and manage large-scale security initiatives will be essential in safeguarding Aurora’s products and ensuring they meet the highest security standards.

The job level is negotiable based on experience. Flexible work locations are available (MTV, SFO, PIT, SEA, DET) for US-based employees (Full remote is not available for this role).

In this role, you will

 - Collaborate with product teams: Work closely with product management, Software and Hardware Development, engineering, and security teams to define security features, assess product risks, prioritize security initiatives, create business and technical use cases, and implement strategic controls that protect both product integrity and user trust.

 - Engage with suppliers and development partners: Work closely with hardware and software suppliers and Tier1 development partners to define and align on cybersecurity features, drive their timely delivery, and ensure that contributions meet Aurora’s security standards and support overall product integrity and user trust.

 - Develop high-level security roadmap(s): Work closely with product and engineering leads to develop high level roadmaps and plans (Business and Technical) which will highlight and document cross-functional dependencies as well as the critical path(s) of various programs and projects.

 - Lead security integration: Develop and execute security assurance, governance, and risk management programs, ensuring they are deeply embedded into all phases of product development from hardware to support applications and that they are aligned with company goals objectives.

 - Monitor and report: Define and report on key performance indicators (KPIs) related to product and security risks, ensuring transparency and data-driven decision-making across the organization.

Required Qualifications

 - 10+ years of experience in Technical Product, Program or Product Management role, in the automotive or AV domain preferred and also cybersecurity experience. 

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a STEM field or equivalent experience.

 - Proven experience developing product strategies, building product use cases, leading large-scale programs with an emphasis on project management, requirements management, and integrating hardware and software features into complex products.   

 - Strong communication and leadership skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate with cross-functional product teams.

 - Hands-on experience participating and directing product development.

Desirable Qualifications

 - Experience building and scaling product programs from the ground up, particularly in product-focused environments or industries with stringent security requirements.

 - Strong knowledge of auto industry security standards and regulations (e.g. ISO21434)

 - Proven ability to lead broad organizational changes.

 - Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex security concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, particularly in a product context.

 - Advanced certifications such as CISSP, CISM, or equivalent
